items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: I got interested in it, I roped my brother John and Joe into it, I got them into it, and then some local kids that were in school with us, I got one of them to play bass and a couple of them played trumpet.

ctx.x: Wow. Was there any rivalry with your brothers regarding music?

No. We’ve always gotten along. We never had any kind of arguments that I can see. Basically I was the first one interested in jazz. I got interested in it, I roped my brother John and Joe into it, I got them into it, and then some local kids that were in school with us, I got one of them to play bass and a couple of them played trumpet. But we never really fought over anything. Even to this day we’re still in kind of an agreement. And it’s kind of unusual. You know I played a club here called The Rex and I know…

items.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021
items.q: We were all in music together, we were all in scouting together, and because of that involvement, Pat and John and I are all Eagle Scouts

ctx.x: Your motivation when you were nine or ten was jumpstarted by your father and your brothers. Did your father try to instill some of that reality in you or was it sort of like just a way for the family to be together?

I think it was more of that, Monk, because we as a family did everything together. We were all in music together, we were all in scouting together, and because of that involvement, Pat and John and I are all Eagle Scouts, because my parents were involved in everything that we do, right? So I believe it was more about the family community, the family commitment, and also at that age someone might say I want to be the president or a fireman or whatever, you know, and of course you’re allowed to say that.
